record.paper_title: Billiard dynamics: A survey with the emphasis on open problems
record.original_question: For an arbitrary Birkhoff billiard table Y, let Φ be the phase space of the billiard map, let P_n be the set of periodic points of period n, and let μ be the Liouville measure on Φ. Is it true that μ(P_n)=0 for every n?

evidence.quote: б) Доказать, что μ(Pn)=0 для всех n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Y\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a smooth strictly convex bounded domain (a Birkhoff billiard table). The billiard map $T$ acts on the phase space
$$\Phi=\{(q,v):q\in\partial Y,\ v\text{ a unit vector pointing inward}\},$$
sending $(q,v)$ to $(q',v')$, where $q'\in\partial Y$ is the next point of intersection of the ray from $q$ in direction $v$ with $\partial Y$, and $v'$ is the reflection of $v$ across the tangent line at $q'$ (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection). Equip $\Phi$ with the Liouville measure $\mu$, the $T$-invariant measure given (in arclength–angle coordinates $(s,\theta)$ with $\theta\in(0,\pi)$ the angle between $v$ and the boundary) by $d\mu=\sin\theta\,ds\,d\theta$.

For each integer $n\ge 2$, let
$$P_n=\{x\in\Phi:T^n(x)=x\}$$
be the set of periodic points of period $n$.

Prove or disprove: for every smooth strictly convex billiard table $Y$ and every integer $n\ge 2$,
$$\mu(P_n)=0.$$
artifact.category_tag: Ivrii's conjecture on periodic billiard orbits
artifact.status_search_result: This is Ivrii's conjecture (1980). It is known to hold in several special cases: real-analytic boundaries, and the cases n=3 (Rychlik, and others) and n=4 (Glutsyuk–Kudryashov, Vorobets); generic algebraic domains have been handled via complex methods. However, for general smooth (non-analytic) boundaries and arbitrary period n, the conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.title: Ivrii's conjecture for some cases in outer and symplectic billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Ivrii's conjecture (1980) predicts that no billiard has a positive-measure set of periodic orbits; partial results prove it for low periods and special classes.
status_evidence.claim: The general conjecture is still open; only partial results for specific periods or analytic/algebraic boundaries are known.

status_evidence.title: No planar billiard possesses an open set of quadrilateral orbits
status_evidence.snippet: Glutsyuk–Kudryashov: no planar billiard has an open set of 4-periodic orbits.
status_evidence.claim: The 4-periodic case of Ivrii's conjecture is established.
